chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Hussain bin Ahmad al-Maliki, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Tawus, year 241

He said: I said to Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him: There is a son of my brother to whom I married my daughter. He drinks intoxicant drinks and mentions divorce abundantly. He said: If he is from your brothers, there is nothing upon him, and if he is from those, then disconnect her from him – for he meant separation. He said: I said: May I be sacrificed for you, has it not been narrated of Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: «Beware from those (females) who have been divorced thrice in one gathering, for indeed, they are ones with husbands»? He said: That refers to your brothers, not those, because the one who lives by the religion of a people is bound by their rulings.

key_terms.دَانَ بِدِينِ قَوْمٍ: Adhered to the religion of a people
key_terms.ذَوَاتُ أَزْوَاجٍ: Ones with husbands (status of being married)

ai.seo_question: How does the ruling for three divorces in one sitting differ between Muslims and non-Muslims according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *talfiq* or adherence to specific jurisprudential schools by distinguishing between 'your brothers' (Shia) and 'those' (likely referring to Sunnis or other sects). He clarifies that the ruling of 'three divorces in one sitting' constituting a final divorce is specific to the latter group's jurisprudence, whereas for the former, it may not be final, demonstrating that one who adopts the religion of a people is bound by their specific legal interpretations (*ahkam*).
